description: A 4 × 4 composite of 16 secondary-electron SEM micrographs of the 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu at.%) low-density steel after aging; every main field carries a 50 μm scale bar and several panels contain a higher-magnification inset with a 10 μm scale bar. Rows are labelled by aging temperature and column by time: row 1, 525 °C − 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 10 h; row 2, 550 °C − 1, 3, 6, 10 h; row 3, 575 °C − 1, 3, 6, 10 h; row 4, 600 °C − 1 h, 600 °C − 6 h, 625 °C − 1 h, 650 °C − 1 h. Green arrows label β-Mn, blue arrows label α-Mn in the 1 h insets at 525/550/575 °C, red text marks "Untransformed α" in the 525 °C − 3 h and 575 °C − 1 h panels, and magenta "New precipitates" arrows point at fine particles in the 10 h panels and in the 625/650 °C panels. With increasing time and temperature the surfaces evolve from an α matrix containing discrete α-Mn/β-Mn particles and needle-like precipitates (insets) to an essentially featureless, uniformly transformed matrix in the long-time and high-temperature panels. The figure demonstrates that the α → β-Mn transformation of the 15Al alloy proceeds fastest at the higher aging temperatures, leaving little resolvable second phase at the 50 μm scale.

observations.observation: The figure is a 4 × 4 array of 16 secondary-electron SEM micrographs, each main field carrying a 50 μm scale bar and several panels including a higher-magnification inset with a 10 μm scale bar.
Panels are labelled with aging conditions: 525 °C (1, 3, 6, 10 h), 550 °C (1, 3, 6, 10 h) and 575 °C (1, 3, 6, 10 h) in rows 1–3, and 600 °C − 1 h, 600 °C − 6 h, 625 °C − 1 h, 650 °C − 1 h in row 4.

Green arrows labelled β-Mn are drawn in the 525 °C − 1 h, 525 °C − 3 h, 525 °C − 6 h, 550 °C − 1 h, 550 °C − 3 h, 550 °C − 6 h, 575 °C − 1 h, 575 °C − 6 h, 600 °C − 1 h, 600 °C − 6 h and 625 °C − 1 h panels.
Blue arrows labelled α-Mn appear only in the 1 h insets at 525 °C, 550 °C and 575 °C, indicating retained α-Mn at short aging times.
Red text 'Untransformed α' with an arrow marks remnant α phase in the 525 °C − 3 h and 575 °C − 1 h panels.
Magenta text 'New precipitates' with arrows points to fine particles in the 10 h panels of the 525, 550 and 575 °C rows and in the 625 °C − 1 h and 650 °C − 1 h panels.
High-magnification insets (e.g. 525 °C − 1 h, 550 °C − 1 h, 575 °C − 1 h, 650 °C − 1 h) reveal needle/plate-like acicular precipitates that are not resolvable in the 50 μm main fields.

The 525 °C − 3 h panel still displays a region explicitly labelled 'Untransformed α', which appears to conflict with the citing text's statement that transformation was almost complete within 3 h at 525 °C; both readings are reported.
The caption states the images are secondary electron images of the 15Al alloy after different aging treatments.
The citing text states that within 3 h of aging at 525 °C the α matrix had been almost completely transformed into β-Mn (Fig. 7).
The citing text attributes the ultrahigh hardness to extensive formation of β-Mn and states β-Mn has an intrinsic hardness of over 10 GPa.
The citing text states that increasing Al content decreases β-Mn precipitation kinetics, with the 17Al and 19Al alloys completing the transformation only after 6 h and 10 h at 550 °C (Figs. 8 and 9).

unreadable_items: Inset scale bars in several panels are only partially legible at the supplied resolution (best read as 10 μm, but some render as only '2 μ' or similar)
Inset phase annotations are too small to read reliably in several panels (e.g. the 525 °C − 3 h and 550 °C − 6 h insets)
Fine precipitate morphology inside the small insets cannot be resolved well enough to describe particle shape quantitatively
